name: Beta 1.0.84
notes: Red planet names now use the same whole-orbit check as the tuning chart and green names: red means ore would overflow somewhere in the orbit

log.t: Red planet names now use the same whole-orbit check as the tuning chart and green names: red means ore would overflow somewhere in the orbit
Stars twinkle more slowly, at random moments
The background stars now show in front of the galaxy and twinkle, and the galaxy is a little brighter
Planet names turn green when they have hauling to spare: a Speed or Cargo point could move to Mine rate and the ships would still keep up
Removed the crew list from the Specialists card: it now shows how many crews are hired, and each crew's quirk sits under its name above the area it controls
Each crew's name now sits above the area it controls: points, perks and training programs
Fixed a crash when hiring an Instructors crew

Removed Handling, Dock training and the − 2 s docking perk and quirk: the 28 seconds of docking, landing and loading are always fixed, and upgrades only speed up the flight. Handling points come back as free points

Mining crews reworked: a planet's points now go into one pool that the Crew Chief (crew 1) allocates across every trait, each point costing a little more than the last. The Shift Crew (crew 2) adds 20 points and swappable perk slots; the Instructors (crew 3) add 20 points and run training programs: Dock training, Prospecting, Deep drilling, Logistics, Advanced shifts and Mentoring. Specialist roles and retraining are replaced: Dockhands and Prospectors become Dock training and Prospecting, and existing saves carry over

Fixed Balance leaving planets short of ships when they have big silos (Ore Silos or Deep Silos): it could push mining a few percent above what the ships carry, so the planet's name turned red. Balance and the chart now account for the silo filling up over time
Tuning chart: only the round handles drag the lines; touching anywhere else on the chart does nothing, so swiping over it scrolls the panel
Planet tab trait panes: the crew-name and Next lines are gone; the planet's total multiplier sits next to each trait's name, and the panes are shorter
Upgrade + and − buttons keep the same size in every state, including Maxed
Maxed upgrade buttons no longer show the 20 / 20 count
Planet tab: the selected planet stays in view in the planet list (after switching tabs, opening the panel, turning or resizing the screen, or a few seconds after you scroll the list yourself)
Tapping a crew, planet, furnace ore or tab that's partly off the edge of its list scrolls the list so it's fully in view; opening a user guide section near the bottom scrolls it into view

Balance keeps ships ahead: income is now worked out over a whole cycle with each planet's real silo, Balance only picks layouts where the ships keep up (then the most income), and when free moves can't get there it offers the cheapest points to buy (To keep up · Add) or says the crews need a hire, retrain or research. The red best-upgrade button and the drag handles use the same, more accurate model

Quieter updates: new versions come out once a day at 4 pm Central and install themselves the next time you open the game; only important updates ask, at most once a day, and the update message lists everything new since your version
Mining teams are now called mining crews throughout the game and the user guide
The Planet tab's Mining teams card is now titled Specialists
Reverted the Mining teams card layout to Beta 1.0.62 (taller trait panes, team name above the chart)

Mining teams card: the chart comes first, then the team picker and the current team's name right above its Mine rate, Speed and Cargo panes; panes are shorter (team multiplier moved into the title row); quirk, perks and Retrain sit below the panes
Tuning chart: the mining handle is on the left edge and the hauling (Speed and Cargo) handle on the right, both with up and down arrows
Mining teams: the Preview button is gone; dragging a handle or Balance shows a preview, and while it's showing the + and − buttons fine-tune it (otherwise they act at once as before)
Planet tab: the Mined vs hauled card is gone; its details (mined and hauled rates, close-pass marker, silo, overflow and sale timer) are now part of the tuning chart in the Mining teams card

Mining teams: a tuning chart in the card shows mining against hauling through the cycle and updates with every change. Preview plans changes with dashed after-lines, cost and income change, then Apply or Cancel. Drag the orange or teal handle to set mining or average hauling and the cheapest points are planned for you; Balance rearranges points for the most income for free
Tapping the credit total switches number style without a message
Numbers: tapping the credit total cycles named (Qa…), letters (aa…) and full words; the Warp tab's Numbers card is gone

Numbers: choose named (Qa, Qi, Sx…) or letter (aa, ab, ac…) names for numbers past a trillion in the Warp tab; full-word numbers are capitalised (1.2 Million); fixed exact powers of a thousand showing as 999 of the size below
Mining teams: the next team can only be hired once the planet's newest team is fully upgraded (20 / 20); the hire panel shows progress toward unlocking it

Retraining: any specialist team can retrain into a new role and pick one of three new quirks (points come back as free points, perks reset, 10 minutes off the job). Price is a quarter of its hire cost and doubles with each paid retrain. The planet the station parks at gets a free retrain, and planets left badly short of ships after a move get Priority Training at 75% off; the parking forecast flags them
Mining team upgrade buttons are back to green and red (with outlined − buttons); other panel buttons stay orange
Main screen: star dust indicator removed (it's in the Warp tab); credits, status lines and the Recenter, Music and Full screen buttons made more compact and consistent
Smelter: opening the tab centres each furnace's ore row on the ore it's smelting, and the Off button sits next to the furnace's name
Every usable button in the panel is now orange (the red best-upgrade and warning buttons keep their colour; disabled buttons fade; toggles fill in when on)
User guide: Tips and tricks moved to the bottom, and every section starts collapsed

Specialist crews: a planet's 2nd and 3rd teams now pick a role (Drillers, Haulers, Dockhands or Prospectors, one of each per planet), are chosen from three named candidates with quirks, and unlock a choice of veteran perks at 10 and 20 upgrades. Dockhands cut docking and loading time and add silo space; Prospectors raise ore yield, strike rich veins and steer probes. Existing second and third teams become Drillers or Haulers with spare points refunded. Economy retuned so pacing stays the same
Planet tab: the planet list stays pinned at the top while you scroll, and switching planets keeps your scroll position (also when tapping a planet in the sky)
User guide in the Warp tab: how every part of the game works, with a Tips and tricks section; shorter Market Surge status line so it fits on one line on small phones

Overdrive is replaced by Market Surge: for 10 minutes everything you sell earns double, up to 10 minutes' worth of extra income, then it recharges for 60 minutes. Mining and ships stay at normal speed, so there are no bottlenecks
